Resource: FHIR Version: R4B (4.3.0) — base resource: Condition, unchanged in structure between R4 and R4B
Design principle — read before using this profile

Description: This is a SPECIALIZATION of Condition for emergency diagnosis staging — do not reuse your generic/routine-visit Condition profile for ED cases.
Comments: One emergency encounter (EMIncidentEncounter/EMPOCEncounter/downstream ED Encounter) is expected to produce MULTIPLE Condition instances over time — one per diagnostic stage — distinguished by category + verificationStatus, never overwritten in place. See the 'Expected Condition Instances per Encounter' section at the bottom of this sheet for how many of each stage to expect.

Description: Optional local identifier for this specific diagnosis entry.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support. Most implementations rely on Condition.id + category + recordedDate for uniqueness rather than a business identifier.

Description: The patient this diagnosis concerns.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) — every Condition instance must reference the same Patient (known or unidentified-temp) as the parent encounter.

Description: The encounter this diagnosis was recorded in — EMIncidentEncounter, EMPOCEncounter, or a downstream ED Encounter.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) — this is the primary linkage your SHA claims pipeline reads to associate a diagnosis with the correct billable encounter and its stage.

Resource: Staging — category & verificationStatus (the core of this profile)

Description: Which diagnostic stage this instance represents. Maps directly to the chief-complaint / working-diagnosis / discharge-diagnosis progression discussed above.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Proposed values: chief-complaint | working-diagnosis | differential-diagnosis | discharge-diagnosis. This is the single most important element on the profile — your SHA claims mapping logic MUST read this before deciding which diagnosis code to submit for adjudication. Also carry the base http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category code (problem-list-item | encounter-diagnosis) as a second Coding within the same CodeableConcept if you need base-spec conformance alongside the local staging value.

Description: Confidence level of this specific diagnosis entry at the time it was recorded.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT — tightened from the base spec's optional binding specifically for this emergency profile. Canonical values: unconfirmed | provisional | differential | confirmed | refuted | entered-in-error. Expected progression: chief-complaint → typically 'unconfirmed' (it's not a diagnosis); working-diagnosis → 'provisional' or 'differential'; discharge-diagnosis → 'confirmed'. NEVER submit a claim against a 'provisional' or 'differential' instance as if it were 'confirmed' — this is a common source of claim rejections.

Description: Whether the condition is currently active.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Typically 'active' for all three emergency stages — 'resolved'/'inactive' are rare in an acute encounter but keep the element populated for consistency with facility-side Condition records that will later track resolution.

Description: The actual diagnosis or complaint code.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. For category=chief-complaint, code a symptom/complaint (SNOMED CT finding or a local symptom ValueSet) rather than forcing an ICD-10 diagnosis code — a chief complaint is not yet a diagnosis. For working-diagnosis/discharge-diagnosis, use ICD-10 consistent with your existing standards stack. FLAG FROM REAL HANDOVER DATA: the source system's condition_id values (e.g. 'ND91.Z') follow an ICD-11 pattern, not ICD-10 — confirm with the vendor and your terminology team which code system is actually authoritative before finalizing this binding; if it's genuinely ICD-11, this ValueSet needs updating across every profile that references diagnosis coding, not just this one.

Description: Triage-linked acuity/severity marker for this diagnosis.
Valueset URL: http://hie.go.ke/fhir/ValueSet/em-diagnosis-severity (local — proposed) or SNOMED CT severity codes (mild | moderate | severe)
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — not every stage will carry a severity marker (rarely meaningful on a chief-complaint), but when present this is what feeds billing tier / SHA benefit classification, so the profile must be able to carry it.

Description: Anatomical site(s) relevant to the diagnosis.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support, but explicitly 0..* (not 0..1) so trauma cases with multiple co-occurring diagnoses across different body sites are supported without forcing an artificial single 'primary site'.

Description: When the condition/symptom is believed to have started, relative to arrival where possible.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — granular timing matters for time-sensitive protocols (stroke/MI 'minutes matter'). Capture relative to EMIncidentEncounter/EMPOCEncounter.period.start where the exact onset time is unknown but time-since-arrival is clinically meaningful.

Description: When THIS diagnosis entry was recorded — distinct from onset.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. This is what lets you reconstruct the staging timeline (chief-complaint recorded at T0, working-diagnosis at T+12min, discharge-diagnosis at T+90min) even when clinical onset itself is unclear or unknown.

Description: When the condition resolved.
Comments: EXCLUDED (Min/Max 0..0) on this profile — resolution timing is not a meaningful concept for an acute emergency diagnosis stage; leave this to the facility-side/inpatient Condition profile if the episode continues.

Resource: Provenance — who recorded / asserted the diagnosis

Description: Who recorded this diagnosis entry — will differ by stage (EMT for working-diagnosis, ED physician for discharge-diagnosis).
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — recommended to always populate in practice, but not forced to Min 1..1 since some system integrations may not reliably capture the individual recorder.

Description: Who originally asserted this — for category=chief-complaint this is often the patient or caller themselves, not a clinician.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support. Useful to distinguish 'patient said chest pain' (asserter=Patient) from 'EMT suspects ACS' (asserter=Practitioner), but not essential to core claims workflow.

Description: Supporting evidence (labs/imaging) that led to a working or discharge diagnosis.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support at the EMS/point-of-care stage; becomes more relevant once the patient reaches facility-based workup (labs/imaging), so expect this to populate later in the episode rather than at EMPOCEncounter.

Description: Free-text clinical notes about this diagnosis entry.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support. Useful for capturing clinician reasoning but should never be the only place a coded severity/category value lives.

Resource: Expected Condition Instances per Encounter (stage multiplicity — not element cardinality)

Description: Expected number of chief-complaint Condition instances per emergency encounter.
Comments: Minimum 1 expected per encounter — this is usually the very first Condition-shaped record created, often derived directly from caller-reported or patient-reported information.

Description: Expected number of working/differential-diagnosis instances per emergency encounter.
Comments: 0..* — zero if the team moves straight from chief-complaint to a confirmed discharge-diagnosis (common in clear-cut cases); multiple instances expected in complex/trauma cases where several differentials are tracked in parallel before narrowing down.

Description: Expected number of discharge-diagnosis instances per emergency encounter.
Comments: 0..* — typically 1, but deliberately not capped at 1: trauma cases legitimately close with multiple co-equal discharge diagnoses and no single 'primary'. Required (at least one) before the encounter/episode can be considered diagnostically closed for claims purposes, but that is an encounter-closure business rule, not a hard FHIR cardinality constraint on this profile.
